entries.title: iPhone users on Google Fi will now get all their voicemails in the Phone app
entries.snippet: Google Fi is changing how iPhone users access their voicemails by enabling voicemail access directly through the native iOS Phone app. Previously, voicemails were accessed via a dedicated tab in the Google Fi app. The rollout of this update began on June 24 and is expected to be completed by July 2, 2025. Starting in August, Google will remove voicemail support from the iOS Google Fi app entirely. Users are advised to download any important voicemails through Google Takeout before August 13, as they will no longer be accessible through the Fi app after this date. Prior to this change, voicemail delivery to the iPhone Phone app was only possible under specific conditions, such as having iOS’s Live Voicemail feature enabled and being within the Fi service area. The update ensures that all voicemails will now consistently appear in the iOS Phone app. This change is part of broader improvements teased by Google in April, including the introduction of a more affordable Unlimited Essentials plan at $35 per month.

entries.title: Prevent Blocked Numbers from Leaving Voicemail on Your Android Device
entries.snippet: This article provides guidance on how to prevent blocked numbers from leaving voicemails on Android devices. While blocking a number typically stops the phone from ringing, it doesn't automatically block voicemails. To fully block voicemails, users must utilize specific carrier apps or third-party solutions. AT&T users can use the free AT&T ActiveArmor app; Verizon customers can temporarily block up to five numbers through their My Verizon account or subscribe to the Verizon Smart Family plan for permanent blocks. T-Mobile offers the Scam Shield app, but voicemail blocking requires a premium subscription. Additionally, the Call Control app is a third-party option that allows users to block calls and voicemails using a "Disconnect" method. For Google Voice users, unwanted voicemails can be sent to the spam folder by marking numbers as spam within the app. The article also answers common questions about identifying if your number is blocked, checking your blocked numbers list, and handling persistent calls from blocked numbers.
